description: Two mystery plants: one green, one tall and pale. Run a real fair test with pots A, B and C, watch ten days in forty seconds, and learn what plants need.

youtube.title: What Do Plants Need? A Real Plant Experiment for Kids | Light and Water | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Same seeds, same pots, same day, so why is one plant green and the other tall and pale? Robo, Cat and Bunny run a fair test: pot A gets light and water, pot B goes in a dark cupboard, pot C gets no water.
Watch ten days in forty seconds, compare the results, and learn what roots, stems and leaves do.
Try at home with a grown-up: cress seeds in three cups. Wash your hands after touching soil and never eat seeds.

do.text: Plant Lab
Welcome to the science fair! Look at these two plants.
This one is short, green and leafy.
This one is tall, skinny and pale yellow.
Same seeds. Same pots. Same day. So what happened?
I want to see the evidence.
Then let's do our own experiment and find out!
First, what do plants need? What do you think?
Light! Plants need light from the sun.
light
Water! Plants need water to drink up.
water
Air! Plants need air, just like you.
air
Space! Room for roots and leaves to grow.
space
And nutrients from the soil. Like vitamins for plants.
soil
Do plants need all of them, or just some?
All of them, to grow well.
But seeds are special. You'll see why.
So which one went missing for the pale plant?
That's the mystery! Fun fact first.
Young sunflowers turn their heads,
following the sun across the sky!
I'm the gardener. I'll keep the lab notebook!
Here's our fair test. Three pots: A, B and C.
Same seeds, same pots, same soil, same number of seeds.
Pot A gets sunlight and a little water every day.
A
Pot A is our control. It gets everything a plant needs.
control
Now, I have an idea.
Pot C goes in the cupboard with no water!
Wait! That changes two things. Light and water.
Then we wouldn't know which change made the difference.
You're right. That's not fair. We change only one thing!
Pot B goes in a dark cupboard, but gets water like A.
So A and B are the same, except for light.
Pot C stays in the sun, but gets no water at all.
So A and C are the same, except for water.
When I say how many things do we change, you say only one!
How many things do we change?
Only one! Great scientists.
Do this with a grown-up.
with a grown-up
They help with windowsills and cupboards.
Scientists make a prediction. That's a smart guess.
prediction
I predict pot A will grow green and strong.
I predict pot C won't grow. It's too thirsty!
A prediction can be wrong.
That's okay. The evidence decides.
And pot B in the dark? Will it sprout? What do you think?
I'm writing every prediction in my notebook.
Let's find out! Bunny, water A and B every day. Never C.
Got it. A and B get water. C gets none.
Now, ten days in forty seconds. Watch the day counter!
Crouch down like a seed, and grow along with pot A!
Day 1
seed
Day 3
sprout
Day 3. Tiny sprouts in A and B. Nothing in C.
Day 5
Day 5. A is short and green. B is taller, thinner and pale.
Day 7
Day 7. A is bushy. B is tall and floppy. C is still dry.
Day 10
Day 10! Let's look closely at all three pots.
Fun fact: some bamboo can grow almost a metre in one day!
Here are the results. Pot A is green and strong.
A green and strong
Pot C has dry soil and no sprouts.
C no sprouts
Compare A and C. Only water was different.
So seeds need water to start growing!
And pot B? It sprouted in the dark, and grew tall and pale.
B tall and pale
Wait. It grew in the dark? I thought plants need light.
Seeds don't need light to sprout.
sprout
They have food stored inside.
But why is the dark one taller?
The young plant was stretching up, looking for light!
Without light, leaves can't make food. So they stay pale.
And the plant gets weak and floppy.
In the dark, stretch up very tall and wobbly, like pot B!
Compare A and B. Only light was different.
Plants need light to grow green and strong!
So water wakes up the seed, and light keeps the plant green.
That's why we needed a fair test. One change, one answer.
So the mystery plant was kept in the dark. Case solved.
And it's all in my lab notebook!
Let's see how a plant uses water and light.
The roots take up water from the soil.
Roots also hold the plant tight in the soil.
The stem carries the water up, like a straw.
The leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant.
Water goes up, sunlight comes down,
and the leaves make food.
That food is a kind of sugar the plant uses to grow.
So plants make their own food. They don't eat soil?
Right. They take in water and nutrients through their roots.
Fun fact: plants give off oxygen.
It's part of the air we breathe!
Crouch down like a seed. Now grow with the chant!
Light up high, water low,
give me space and watch me grow!
Roots dig down, stems grow tall,
leaves catch sunlight, that's not all!
Light up high, water low, give me space and watch me grow!
Challenge! Is each test fair or not fair?
One: two pots in the sun. One gets water, one gets none.
Fair! Only one thing changes: water.
Two: one pot in the sun with water,
one in the dark with none.
Not fair! Two things change: light and water.
Three: same pots, but one has 3 seeds and one has 30.
Not fair! The number of seeds changed too.
Four: two pots in the sun. A little water, or a flood.
Fair! It tests how much water. Only one thing changes.
Change one thing, keep the rest the same. That's fair.
Quiz time! Which pot got no water? What happened?
Pot C. Its seeds did not sprout.
Why did pot B grow tall and pale?
It stretched for light, and leaves need light to make food.
What makes a test fair?
Change only one thing!
Name three things plants need.
Light, water, air, space and nutrients from soil. Any three!
Here's our green and strong plant!
Evidence wins.
Try cress seeds in three cups with a grown-up.
with a grown-up
Don't eat the seeds!
Check your cups every day at the same time,
and draw what you see.
